title: feat: t4 package LibreCrawl for Cloudron (GH#1)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #1 (t4).

- Packages LibreCrawl `05a1372de8334ca18dec0bc1f7470c62901a9418` on the digest-pinned Cloudron 6.0.0 base for Cloudron 9.1+.
- Adds signed-in-only startup, verified first admin, persistent 0600 signing key, SQLite state, operator account commands and consistent pre-upgrade snapshots.
- Adds daily configurable finished-crawl retention with cascading pages/links/issues/queue deletion and opt-in vacuum, without patching upstream source.
- Adds Chromium-only installation, original 256×256 / 1188×396 artwork, operator guides, static checks, pinned release/linked-issue callers, and opt-in GHCR/catalog attestations.
- Key files: `CloudronManifest.json`, `Dockerfile`, `start.sh`, `bin/librecrawl-user`, `bin/librecrawl-retention`, `scripts/publish-cloudron-catalog.sh`, `.github/workflows/`, `docs/`, `test/package-test.sh`. Reference pattern: cloudron-netbird-app.

## Runtime Testing

**Level: runtime-verified. Risk: critical (accounts, signing key, deletion).**

Verified tree at final head `b0aa167ead09fa7ae9fcb48a06bb9a54c4bc2126`; the helper squashed checkpoint commits without changing file contents. Local image ID: `sha256:dee7a167f45f295bfb3861647c9066c0fa913133f314008f3836645f19d24872` (amd64).

- `cloudron-package-helper.sh validate` and `check-compatibility`: pass.
- `bash test/package-test.sh`: pass.
- `shellcheck start.sh bin/librecrawl-user bin/librecrawl-retention scripts/*.sh test/*.sh`: zero findings.
- `actionlint` on all three new workflows: pass. No markdownlint configuration is present.
- `docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t librecrawl-cloudron:gh1 .`: pass.
- Disposable Docker runtime used `--network none --read-only`, a named `/app/data` volume, and tmpfs at `/tmp` and `/run`; server and HTTP client ran together inside the invocation. A disposable two-page HTTP server was the only crawl target. No external site or production data was crawled. Temporary verification code is not shipped as test infrastructure.

| Required product path | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `/login` | HTTP 200 |
| First admin sign-in | Success, verified admin tier |
| Anonymous API / guest / registration / empty password | Refused |
| Account add / tier / reset-password / list | Pass; stdin passwords, verified service account, old password refused after reset |
| Plugin-style login, save_settings (`maxUrls: 50`), start_crawl, crawl_status, crawls/list, load | Completed crawl ID 1; two pages persisted |
| `export_stream?type=urls&format=csv` | HTTP success, **2 data rows** |
| Restart with existing cookie | Same cookie still authenticated; settings, crawl, signing key and initial password preserved |
| Secret and bootstrap password permissions | 0600 |
| Operator-changed admin tier | Preserved through restart, not forcibly promoted |
| Changed-pin SQLite online snapshot | Integrity `ok`, crawl present; repeated transition refresh includes newly created user |
| 0-day retention, vacuum enabled | Deleted 1 completed crawl, **2 pages / 2 links / 20 issues / 1 queue row → all zero**; running crawl preserved; vacuum succeeds |
| Invalid retention days / LOCAL_MODE / DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_AUTH / DEMO_MODE | Nonzero exit, fail closed |
| Catalog publisher | Real Cloudron CLI 8.2.6 init/add/update/verify passes on an ephemeral catalog; duplicate version rejected without modifying it; no publication |

Installed runtime verified: Python 3.14.4, Flask 2.3.3, Waitress 3.0.2, Playwright 1.64.0, bcrypt 4.1.2, requests 2.31.0. Upstream account/cleanup exports were confirmed against that image. Upstream main was checked on 2026-10-14 and still equals the pinned commit.

## Limitations and remaining qualification

- A supplementary Chromium render attempt failed under QEMU amd64-on-arm64 with signal 5 / unusable GPU process. The browser and dependencies are installed, but **native-amd64 JS rendering is not verified here**. This runner limitation is documented, not hidden by patching upstream flags. Native rendering and live Cloudron install/upgrade/backup-restore/plugin qualification remain t5.
- Upstream has no private-address filter; only trusted accounts are safe. Ingress TLS does not isolate outbound crawls. README, security policy, post-install message and packaging notes warn about this.
- Upstream UI/API deletion still leaves orphan child rows because its normal connections do not enable foreign keys. The package fixes only its retention process; an upstream follow-up is recorded in packaging notes.
- The issue's repository-wide secret-pattern check matches its own literal example in the **pre-existing, unchanged** `todo/tasks/t4-brief.md:214`; changed package files contain neither private-key material nor a `SECRET_KEY=` assignment. No secret or generated catalog was committed.
- Catalog PR preflight passed on the previous checkpoint. The new `pull_request_target` linked-issue caller cannot run from PR-head code before its first merge to the default branch; this is repository bootstrap, not a bypass. Remaining exact-head remote CI/review is handled by the merge gate.

## Decisions and acceptance mapping

- No upstream source patch, no Cloudron proxy-auth wall, no local/guest/skip-auth/demo modes.
- State is `/app/data`; consistent SQLite snapshots include WAL data and retain two upstream-pin snapshots.
- Cleanup enables cascading foreign keys on its process-local adapter before calling upstream `cleanup_old_crawls()`.
- Image/catalog publication requires explicit operator `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true` plus release credentials. This PR does not publish, install on a live Cloudron, change another repository, or hand-write a catalog.
- Operator hand-off in `docs/PUBLISHING.md` covers `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT`, librecrawl-test, restart/upgrade/restore checks, native Chromium, GHCR visibility and Community Apps submission.
- Independent read-only review inspected security/storage/publication and artwork. Both actionable findings (admin re-promotion and stale repeated-pin snapshot) were repaired and runtime-verified. Artwork dimensions/appearance were independently inspected; original provenance is documented in `DESIGN.md`.

title: fix: t5 run LibreCrawl under tini and record live qualification (GH#2)
body:
## Summary

For #2 (t5). The package is not published yet; this PR records the live qualification and fixes the one defect it found.

- **Fix:** run LibreCrawl under `tini` as PID 1. `Dockerfile` installs `tini`; `start.sh` now execs `/usr/bin/tini -- gosu cloudron:cloudron … main.py`. Under upstream as PID 1, JavaScript crawls left Chromium helper processes defunct until restart (five after three crawls). tini reaps them and forwards SIGTERM, so upstream's shutdown handler still saves running crawls as `paused`.
- **Docs:** `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md` records the live qualification: checks passed, memory sizing, restart and resume, scheduled retention, process supervision, and upstream crawl behaviour clients must allow for (`crawlDelay` ignored on HTML crawls, `jsUserAgent`, HEAD-check rows counted in results, slow links export). `docs/README.md` gains the resume endpoint, client caveats, measured memory and when to raise the limit, plus retention sizing. `docs/PUBLISHING.md` explains on-server builds for unpublished qualification installs. `CHANGELOG.md` gets an Unreleased entry.
- **TODO.md:** t4 marked complete (`pr:#4`) with `task-complete-helper.sh`.
- **No manifest change:** the 2 GiB default holds one 5,000-page HTML crawl (peak 1.16 GiB, including load and export), so it stays; the README says when to raise it. The version stays `0.1.0` (never published).

Reference pattern: cloudron-netbird-app (docs layout, release/catalog workflows).

## Runtime Testing

**Level: runtime-verified. Risk: medium** (PID 1 and signal handling decide whether running crawls survive a restart).

Disposable Cloudron 10.0.5 install (x86_64), image built on the server from this branch's tree with `cloudron update` (CLI 8.2.6). Docs-only commits after `7ca54d4` do not change the image.

- PID 1 is `/usr/bin/tini -- gosu cloudron:cloudron /app/code/venv/bin/python main.py --disable-register --disable-guest`; the Python process runs as `cloudron`.
- **Reaping:** three JavaScript crawls on this build (one and three browser pages; 6 URLs and 5 links each, loaded and exported via the API): `ps` shows 0 defunct processes, against 5 after three crawls before tini.
- **SIGTERM:** restarted mid-crawl on this build. The log shows `GRACEFUL SHUTDOWN` → `Saving crawl …` → `All crawls saved successfully`; the crawl was listed `paused` (2,990 rows), and `POST /api/crawls/<id>/resume` returned success and the crawl completed.
- **After update:** health `healthy`; anonymous `/api/user/info` 401; `/` → 302 `/login`; `POST /api/register` refused; service account signs in; signing key unchanged since install; all saved crawls listed.
- **Retention:** the qualification-only two-minute schedule and `CRAWL_RETENTION_DAYS=1` are reverted. Manifest schedule is `0 3 * * *` and the scheduler job was recreated; `/app/data/env` has `CRAWL_RETENTION_DAYS=90`, `CRAWL_VACUUM=false`, mode 600.
- **Static checks:** `bash test/package-test.sh`, `cloudron-package-helper.sh validate`, and `check-compatibility` pass; `shellcheck start.sh` has zero findings; `markdownlint --disable MD013` on the changed Markdown is clean.

Earlier qualification evidence is summarised in `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md` → "Live qualification (t5)": the 5,000-page synthetic crawl (19,781 URL rows, 397,953 links), memory, export timings, backup and restore, and retention deleting with zero orphan rows.

## Not in this PR (operator steps for #2)

- **Publication:** the `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` secret, the `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED` variable and GHCR visibility are not configured. With the variable unset, merging only validates main and publishes nothing.
- **SEO Pro Stats:** a scheduled import can only be tested once the plugin's crawler connection is released.
- **Community Apps:** submission comes after publication.

title: fix: t5 create the GitHub release from the catalog workflow (GH#2)
body:
## Summary

LibreCrawl 0.1.0 is published (catalog run 38837922383: image, catalog,
attestations, `v0.1.0` tag), but it has no GitHub release. This adds a
release job to the catalog workflow that creates the release after
publication and repairs a missing one on later main runs.

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish.yml` commits the catalog as
`chore: publish Cloudron package 0.1.0` with GitHub's skip-CI marker and
pushes the `v0.1.0` tag on that commit. GitHub skips push-triggered workflows
when the head commit carries that marker, tag pushes included, so
`cloudron-package-release.yml` never ran: `gh run list` shows no run for the
tag and `gh release list` is empty.
The NetBird package has the same tag caller; its last run was v2.0.4, and
later releases come from a release step in its catalog workflow.

## Change

- `scripts/create-github-release.sh <version>`: reads everything from the
  version tag. It requires the tag on `origin/main`, a published catalog
  entry pinned to a `ghcr.io/marcusquinn/cloudron-librecrawl-app@sha256:`
  digest, an anonymous `docker buildx imagetools inspect` of that image, and
  `gh attestation verify` of the tag's catalog against this workflow on
  `refs/heads/main`. Then it creates the release if missing. Notes: package
  version, upstream commit and the version's `CHANGELOG` section.
- Workflow: preflight sets `reconcile=true` when publication is enabled on
  main and the manifest version is already in the catalog (never rebuilt).
  The new `release` job runs after a successful publish or on reconcile, with
  `contents: write` and `attestations: read` only; PRs still only validate.
- `test/package-test.sh` syntax-checks the script and asserts the workflow
  calls it. `docs/PUBLISHING.md` step 7 and recovery text describe the
  real flow; also fixes the remaining MD013 line in that file. It now also
  warns that only the catalog commit may carry the skip-CI marker: GitHub
  honours it anywhere in a head commit message, so a merge or PR head that
  quotes it skips the release job. `CHANGELOG.md` records the fix under
  Unreleased.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on all package scripts, `bash test/package-test.sh`,
  `actionlint`, and `markdownlint-cli2` on the changed Markdown: clean.
- The script's tag checks run locally against `v0.1.0`: tag `f938e4e` is
  on main and its catalog pins `sha256:b30adbe2…c4e91c` as published.
- `gh attestation verify` passes for the catalog and the
  `oci://` image with `--signer-workflow …/cloudron-catalog-publish.yml
  --source-ref refs/heads/main` (run 38837922383); the image index resolves
  with `docker buildx imagetools inspect`.
- The first head commit quoted the marker in its body, so this workflow's PR
  validation did not run for it; the follow-up commit's plain message runs
  it. Merge with a squash body that does not quote the marker.
- After merge, the push to main runs preflight with `reconcile=true`, and
  the release job creates `v0.1.0` as `github-actions[bot]`. This proves
  the repair path end to end.

For #2
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

## Summary

Add `ignore: - dependency-name: "marcusquinn/aidevops*"` to the `github-actions` update entries in `.github/dependabot.yml`.

## Why

aidevops reusable-workflow callers pin `uses:` to a release SHA together with a matching `with.aidevops_ref` input. aidevops releases several times a day, and Dependabot bumps only the `uses:` SHA, so each release produced a stale PR that also broke the pairing. Those pins are advanced together by `aidevops sync-workflows --force-ref`.

Other GitHub Actions and ecosystems keep their existing Dependabot schedule.
